name: Great Lakes (Lake Michigan)
blurb: Cold deep lake where invasive mussels, alewife and stocked salmon reshaped the web.

sources.title: USGS: Changes in the Lake Michigan food web following dreissenid mussel invasions

notes: The story and why it matters come from the Wikipedia articles listed below (Lake Michigan, Alewife (fish), Sea lamprey). Individual species and links have not been checked one by one. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.

nodes.desc: A fish-eating raptor of the lakeshore that takes live and dead fish.

link_ideas.what: Chinook salmon were introduced to Lake Michigan from Pacific stocks in 1967

story: Lake Michigan is the world's largest lake lying fully in one country. Overfishing and sea lamprey wiped out lake trout, so alewives grew in number unchecked. Pacific salmon were later introduced as predators. Now alewives feed Chinook salmon, lake trout and cormorants.
matters: Joined to Lake Huron through the Straits of Mackinac, it acts as one lake, the largest body of fresh water on Earth by surface area. Introduced fish now support a popular salmon sport fishery.
